summary: 30-foot pole observation tower and cabin built 1934 in Idaho County; destroyed in the 1940s per most sources. A disputed 1925 cabin; nothing described on site today.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in the 1940s. No source describes what remains at the site.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts site lists a log cabin with a cupola in 1925, from an undated inventory. The Forest Service lists and the Idaho and firelookout.com pages date the 30-foot pole tower and cabin to 1934. The story gives 1934 for the tower and calls the 1925 cabin disputed.

notes_for_editor: Four sources agree on a 30-foot pole observation tower and cabin in 1934 (cites 2 to 5, including the Selway-Bitterroot list, whose Wahoo (Squaw) row gives the same 1934 date and 1940s destruction), and all five that give a status date the destruction to the 1940s. The Nez Perce NF list says it draws on Ray Kresek's book and other sources, so these agreements are not fully independent. The 1925 log cabin appears only on the Forest Lookouts site, citing an undated inventory. A Spokane Historical photo from 1960 is captioned 'Squaw Peak Lookout' and places it in the Bitterroot NF, which fits poorly with the 1957 transfer to Nez Perce NF and the 1940s destruction; it may show a different Squaw Peak, so the story does not count it as evidence the tower survived. The FFLA list also has a separate 'Squaw Peak' (Idaho/Lemhi, 45.52967 -114.60491, Ground Gone) that is a different record and was not used. The Idaho page lists a hike-in and wilderness context, but no current access, remains or staffing information. The Forest Service Selway-Bitterroot list is a list of lookouts, not a statement of the site's legal status, so the story says only that it includes the site.
